links.reason: Acts repeats “kill me as you killed the Egyptian”; Exodus has the man say it to Moses, who was then afraid.
Acts says Moses “fled to the land of Midian”; Exodus says he fled from Pharaoh and settled “in the land of Midian.”
Acts has God say “I have heard their groaning”; Exodus says God “heard their groaning” and remembered His covenant.
Acts repeats “Take off your sandals” and “the place where you are standing is holy ground”; Exodus gives them as God’s words.
Matthew repeats “I am the God of Abraham” from Exodus, then adds “not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
Mark says God told Moses, “I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac”; Exodus gives these words, and Moses hides his face.
Luke says Moses calls the Lord “the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac”; in Exodus, God says “I am the God of your father.”
Acts speaks of “The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob”; in Exodus, God says “I am the God of your father.”
Acts repeats “I am the God of your fathers”; Exodus has “I am the God of your father,” and Moses hides his face.
Acts repeats “I have indeed seen the oppression of My people in Egypt”; Exodus has the same words, with “affliction” for “oppression.”
Acts says “have come down to deliver them”; Exodus says “I have come down to rescue them” from the Egyptians.
Matthew repeats “the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”; in Exodus, God tells Moses to say these words to the Israelites.
Mark repeats “the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”; in Exodus, God says of it, “This is My name forever.”
Luke says Moses calls the Lord “the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”; in Exodus, God says, “This is My name forever.”
Acts names “the God of our fathers”; in Exodus, God tells Moses to say to the Israelites, “the God of your fathers.”
Acts repeats “the God of your fathers”; Exodus has these words from God, and adds “This is My name forever.”
Romans repeats “raised you up for this very purpose”; Exodus continues “that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
Luke says “Every firstborn male shall be consecrated to the Lord”; Exodus has God say “Consecrate to Me every firstborn male.”
2 Corinthians repeats “he who gathered much had no excess”; in Exodus, the people measured it by the omer.
Acts says “You made the heaven and the earth and the sea”; Exodus says the LORD made “the heavens and the earth and the sea.”
Acts says God “made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them”; Exodus says the LORD made them in six days.
Revelation repeats “made the heavens and the earth and the sea”; Exodus says the LORD made them in six days.
Matthew repeats “Honor your father and mother” as God’s word; Exodus adds “so that your days may be long in the land.”
Matthew repeats “honor your father and mother”; Exodus has the same words, then a promise of long days in the land.
Mark says Moses said “Honor your father and your mother”; Exodus has “Honor your father and mother,” with a promise of long days.

Luke lists “honor your father and mother” among the commandments; Exodus has the same words, then a promise of long days.
Ephesians repeats “Honor your father and mother” and calls it “the first commandment with a promise”; Exodus gives the promise of long days.
Ephesians says “that you may have a long life on the earth”; Exodus says “so that your days may be long in the land.”
Matthew says “Do not murder” was said to the ancients; Exodus has “You shall not murder.”

Mark lists “Do not murder” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not murder.”

Mark lists “do not commit adultery” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not commit adultery.”
Luke lists “Do not commit adultery” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not commit adultery.”
Romans lists “Do not commit adultery” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not commit adultery.”
James says He who said “Do not commit adultery” also said “Do not murder”; Exodus says “You shall not commit adultery.”
Matthew has Jesus list “do not steal”; Exodus says “You shall not steal.”
Mark lists “do not steal” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not steal.”
Luke lists “do not steal” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not steal.”
Romans lists “Do not steal” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not steal.”
Matthew has Jesus repeat “do not bear false witness”; Exodus adds “against your neighbor.”
Mark lists “do not bear false witness” among the commandments; Exodus adds “against your neighbor.”
Luke lists “do not bear false witness” among the commandments; Exodus adds “against your neighbor.”
Romans says the law said “Do not covet”; Exodus says “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house.”
Romans lists “Do not covet” among the commandments; Exodus says “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house.”
Matthew repeats “Anyone who curses his father or mother”; Exodus says such a person “must surely be put to death.”
Mark repeats “Anyone who curses his father or mother”; Exodus says such a person “must surely be put to death.”
Matthew repeats “Eye for eye and tooth for tooth”; Exodus has “eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.”
Acts says it is written, “Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people”; Exodus has “curse the ruler of your people.”
Hebrews repeats “This is the blood of the covenant,” the words Moses says in Exodus as he splatters the blood on the people.
Hebrews repeats “according to the pattern shown you on the mountain” as a warning to Moses; Exodus has the same command.
Acts repeats “Make us gods who will go before us” said to Aaron; Exodus has the people gather around Aaron and say it.
1 Corinthians repeats that the people “sat down to eat and drink” and “got up to indulge in revelry”; Exodus says the same after offerings.
Acts repeats “Make us gods who will go before us”; in Exodus, a man says they told him this.
Romans repeats “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy”; Exodus has the LORD say it, along with “I will proclaim My name.”
2 Corinthians says Moses “would put a veil over his face”; Exodus says Moses would “put the veil back over his face.”
Acts repeats the man’s question “Who made you ruler and judge over us?”; Exodus has the same words, and Moses is afraid.
2 Corinthians says God will “dwell with them” and “be their God”; Exodus says He will “dwell among the Israelites and be their God.”
